exercise.name: Incline Y-Raise
library_steps: Lie chest-down on an incline bench, a light dumbbell in each hand.
With thumbs up, raise your arms forward and out into a Y shape.
Lower them slowly until they hang straight down.
exercise.one_line_summary: Chest down on a 30 deg incline bench: light dumbbells hang straight down (start), then straight arms rise forward and out into a Y, about 40 deg either side of the head line, level with the torso, thumbs up (end).

setup.target: Low incline, chest on the pad, chin past the top, feet on the floor.
Light dumbbells, thumbs pointing up at the top.

movement.measure: arm angle in torso frame (elev: 0 = along the side toward the feet, 180 = overhead)
movement.end: about 140 (Y, in line with the torso)

movement.measure: angle of each arm from the head line
still, feet on the floor either side of the seat

muscles.role: Library primary. Prone overhead raise in line with the lower trapezius gave the highest lower-trap and among the highest middle-trap EMG (S1).
Rotate the shoulder blade up as the arm passes overhead.
Lifts the arm against gravity in prone raises (~42% MVIC in prone horizontal abduction, S2).
Library secondary; elevates the arm in the Y.

mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Shoulders ride up as the arms rise.
mistakes.why_it_matters: Upper traps take over from the lower traps.

mistakes.mistake: Lifting the chest off the pad
mistakes.what_it_looks_like: Torso arches up to get the arms higher.

sources.citation: Ekstrom RA, Donatelli RA, Soderberg GL. 2003. Surface electromyographic analysis of exercises for the trapezius and serratus anterior muscles. J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 33(5):247-258.
sources.what_it_gave: 30 subjects, 10 exercises: prone arm raise overhead in line with the lower trapezius = highest lower-trap EMG and tied highest middle-trap EMG.

sources.citation: Kim S, Kang M. 2020. Influence of pre-emptive scapular posterior tilt on scapular muscle activation and scapulohumeral movements during shoulder horizontal abduction in the prone position. J Int Acad Phys Ther Res 11(4):2173-2177.
sources.what_it_gave: Prone raises load lower trap (58-69%), middle trap (~50%) and posterior deltoid (38-42%) MVIC; posterior tilt raises lower-trap share.
Chest-down on an incline bench, thumbs up, raise forward and out into a Y, lower until arms hang.

clip_check.check: End: arms in a Y, in line with the torso
clip_check.target: 30-45 deg from head line; within 10 deg of the torso plane
handle index end above pinky end

clip_check.check: Chest on the pad; feet on the floor
Upper back the strongest red in both pictures
